solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old sponge, superb one that's reversible

indicators.note: something reversible can be turned the other way round, so the phrase before it is read from its end

parts.note: tops is slang for the very best
one stands for another sponge, that is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A sponge from the past is praised as superb and two-sided, as if bought for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: A superb sot is a 'tops sot', and read backwards that becomes TOSSPOT; 'one' points back to 'sponge', meaning a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is a dated word for a habitual drunkard, and sponge is slang for someone who soaks up liquor.

clue.text: People tangling with judge in unimportant matter, seeing old man's beard

indicators.note: in places the preceding phrase inside the word for unimportant matter

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something of no importance
to ravel is to tangle, so those who do it are ravellers
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: People fight with a judge over a trivial matter, all because of an old man's beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' tempts a solver to write TRAVELLERS at once, but the people are those who tangle, and the toy wraps around them and the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is the wild clematis, whose fluffy seed heads give it the common name old man's beard.

clue.text: Die from cold that black stuff caught by hanky carries over

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means turned upside down, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so the substance in the hanky takes the cold abbreviation inside

parts.note: what a handkerchief catches
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone dies of a cold, the black stuff in the hanky a grim sign.
explanation.walkthrough: MUCUS holds C, B goes in front, and the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way, and in particular to die of an illness or injury.

clue.text: Phosphorus explosive attached to arrow in armour

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
HE stands for high explosive
on can mean attached to, as in a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: A phosphorus explosive is fixed to an arrow fired at armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armour' here is armory, the study of heraldic arms, not body armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheon is the heraldic charge of a broad arrowhead, so it is an arrow in coats of arms.

clue.text: Cut down nettle, chopping around group standing for creation, preservation and destruction

definitions.text: group standing for creation, preservation and destruction

parts.note: to trim is to cut down

indicators.note: chopping means cutting off, so the abbreviation for around is removed from the plant name

parts.note: Urtica is the nettle genus
CA, circa, means around

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts back nettles around a group of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Around here is the Latin circa, which is chopped out of the nettle's botanical name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trimurti is the Hindu triad of Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

clue.text: Ruined fortress rebuilt as a dam

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old fortress is reconstructed as a dam, a civil-engineering reuse of ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Masada is the hilltop stronghold in Israel destroyed by the Romans and now an archaeological ruin.

clue.text: Italian house's primitive charm saving lowest quarter

indicators.note: saving means except, and in a down answer the lowest quarter is the bottom fourth of the word, which is left off

parts.note: medicine in the sense of magic, as in a medicine man

explanation.surface: An Italian house has a rustic charm except in its basement.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDICINE has eight letters, so its lowest quarter is the final two, NE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the ruling family of Renaissance Florence, and house here means a noble dynasty.

clue.text: Rider's spiked wheel very easily almost covers engine's hum

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so the sound goes inside
almost means not quite all, so the phrase for very easily loses its last letter

parts.note: so well means very easily
a smooth-running engine purrs

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist's spiked wheel nearly drowns the engine's hum.
explanation.walkthrough: SO WELL drops its last L and holds PURR after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur rowel is the small spiked revolving wheel at the end of a horse rider's spur.

clue.text: Diamonds and pound secured by a measure of cleverness for local capital in Syria

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: something secured by another is held firmly within it, so the word for pound goes inside

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient
to pound is to mash or crush

explanation.surface: Diamonds and sterling are locked away by a clever thief in a Syrian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound is not money but a verb, to crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimashq is the Arabic name used locally for Damascus, the capital city of Syria.

clue.text: When covered, bedding most of very large milkweed

indicators.note: bedding something is setting it into place, so one word is laid inside another

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
clad means clothed or covered

indicators.note: most of something is all but a small part, so the last letter of the next word goes

parts.note: epic means huge in scale

explanation.surface: Something very large is tucked under covers in a bed, an odd gardening scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When covered' reads as one phrase, but when and covered are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Asclepiad is a botanical name for any plant of the milkweed family, after the genus Asclepias.

clue.text: Group that drops keys in the middle of soul music

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the middle of the following words rather than being built from their meanings

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A band changes key during a soul song.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'keys' are not musical: they are the winged seeds some trees shed, and 'group' is a botanical genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulmus is the elm genus, a group of trees that sheds winged seeds, which are called keys.

clue.text: Itchy palms to shakes, having swallowed unknown blood pressure drug

indicators.note: swallowing something takes it inside, so the letter for unknown joins the other letters
shaking something jumbles it, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Itchy palms and the shakes after swallowing an unknown pill suggest a medical scare.
explanation.definitionFit: A sympatholytic drug blocks the sympathetic nervous system and is used to lower high blood pressure.

clue.text: Inter Milan's final comes after spell in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for spell is turned backwards

parts.note: a rune is a magic spell or charm

indicators.note: the final of a word is its closing letter, so only the end of the city name is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of Milan

explanation.surface: Inter Milan's last game comes after a spell in which a player has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter Milan' looks like the football club; Inter is the definition, a verb meaning bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To enurn is to place ashes in an urn, which is a form of burial, the sense of inter.

clue.text: Not baptised before church, rector initially breaks agreement after shortening Mass

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters go into the shortened word
shortening a word cuts its end off, so the word for agreement loses its last letter

parts.note: in unison means in agreement
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of rector
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A rector breaks a church agreement by cutting short the Mass, and someone goes unbaptised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' tempts a solver to start with UN as a separate piece, but here it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom was the white robe of a newly christened baby, so unchrisom describes someone who has not been christened.

clue.text: Operatic parts left one cold, all but the first in review

indicators.text: all but the first in review
indicators.note: a review looks back, and all but the first means every letter of the word except its opening one is turned round

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one
bitter weather is very cold

explanation.surface: A critic reviewing an opera's roles was left cold by everything except the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER keeps its B in place while the rest is read backwards, giving BRETTI after L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Libretti are the texts of operas, and 'parts' here means the words written for singers to perform.

clue.text: With no love for Portuguese resort, visited weaver

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so having none means the round letter is taken out

parts.note: Estoril is a resort town near Lisbon
to do a place is to visit it, as in 'we did Rome'

explanation.surface: Someone who once had no love for a Portuguese resort went there anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means O, from the zero score in tennis; to do a place is a casual way of saying you toured it.
explanation.definitionFit: An estrildid is a member of the family of small finches called waxbills or weaver finches.

clue.text: More than once, quality assurance protects western homeland

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: QA is the usual abbreviation for quality assurance
W is the abbreviation for western
the piece just built is written a second time

explanation.surface: Repeated quality checks keep the Western world safe.
explanation.walkthrough: QwaQwa was a homeland set aside for black South Africans under apartheid; 'More than once' asks for the whole construction twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Under apartheid South Africa created nominally self-governing 'homelands', or bantustans, and QwaQwa was one of these territories.

clue.text: As Piers said, crucial sign of online approval

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for crucial is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: key means crucial, and quay is pronounced the same way
a like is the thumbs-up on social media

explanation.surface: Piers, perhaps a presenter, says that getting a like online is all-important.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers looks like a man's name, but it is the plural noun: landing stages.
explanation.definitionFit: Piers are structures like quays, so something resembling piers can be described as quaylike.

clue.text: Fried food: the object is to flip on eggs

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the phrase for 'the object is' is read backwards

parts.note: the object is → it is → it's

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: when frying, the trick is to flip the eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed after the eggs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated potato shallow-fried into a crisp cake.

clue.text: Tablets with 25 sheets of paper, one over a page?

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so ES is several
a quire is 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A stationery order: tablets plus 25 sheets of paper, one more than a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' seems to mean a sheet of paper, but it is the boy servant in a knight's household.
explanation.definitionFit: In chivalry a page was promoted to squire, so an esquire ranks one step above a page.

clue.text: Uneasy driver under instruction beside motorway stop violently seizes

indicators.note: seizing something means taking hold of it, so the word for stop clasps the other letters inside

parts.note: to quash is to suppress forcefully
a learner driver displays an L plate
the M1 motorway, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A nervous learner driver near the motorway sees someone stopped by force.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, with its digit read as a letter; learner drivers in Britain carry L plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualmish means feeling queasy or troubled by misgivings, from qualm, a sudden pang of doubt or sickness.

clue.text: Don's in Hawaii, getting up in line with consistent bed height

indicators.note: in a down answer, getting up means rising, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: HI is the postal code for Hawaii
a capo is a Mafia don; 's makes it plural-sounding CAPOS, read as 'capo is'

explanation.surface: A Mafia don is in Hawaii, rising early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don's in' is read as 'don is in': a Mafia don goes inside the state's postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopach is a contour line on a geological map joining points where a rock bed has equal thickness.

clue.text: Question Time hosts four geniuses centrally that could be worsted

indicators.note: hosting someone is having them within, so the outer pair of letters surround the rest

parts.note: Q for question
the Roman numeral for four

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle letters of the word just before it

parts.note: the two central letters of geniuses
T for time

explanation.surface: The BBC's Question Time panel features four geniuses who could still be beaten in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Question Time is a BBC political panel show. 'Worsted' is not defeated but the woollen yarn: qiviut is fibre that could be spun into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Qiviut is the soft underwool of the musk ox, a fibre that can be spun into yarn such as worsted.

clue.text: In Notre-Dame, I pack in years, holding Irish prayer bead

parts.note: Notre-Dame suggests France, where I is je

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the phrase for pack in wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: to pack in is to give up
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: A visitor to Notre-Dame crams years of Irish devotion into a rosary.
explanation.walkthrough: Notre-Dame sets the language as French, so the I is translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Jequirity is the bright red seed of Indian liquorice, strung and used as beads in rosaries.

clue.text: Scots bully foolish people from the east

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means right to left, so the word is backwards

parts.note: loons are crazy or silly people

explanation.surface: A Scottish bully finds a crowd of fools coming from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Snool is a Scots verb meaning to domineer over or keep in subjection, which is what a bully does.

clue.text: Husband in evil action cut up string of prayer beads

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from the bottom upward
in places the abbreviation inside the rest
cutting a word trims its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: abuse is cruel or wrongful treatment
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband caught in an evil act is badly cut up.
explanation.walkthrough: ABUSE loses its E and is reversed to SUBA, with H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A subha is the Muslim rosary, a string of beads used to count recitations in prayer.

clue.text: Younger drip daughter's torn apart no more

parts.note: YR is a standard abbreviation for younger
an IV is an intravenous drip
D for daughter, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A younger daughter, a bit of a drip, has been torn apart and no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No more' marks the definition as obsolete: yrivd is a Spenserian past participle of rive.
explanation.definitionFit: Rive is an old verb meaning to tear or split, and yrivd is Spenser's archaic past participle form of it.

clue.text: Identify current part of Ukraine cell that's unlike neighbours

parts.note: to ID someone is to identify them
I is the symbol for electric current
an oblast is a province or region of Ukraine

explanation.surface: An agent identifies a current resident of a Ukrainian region as a sleeper cell, out of step with the locals.
explanation.definitionFit: An idioblast is a plant cell whose form or contents differ markedly from the surrounding tissue.

clue.text: Bluey-green substance R&D used to replace centre of soft, smooth surface

indicators.note: the given letters are swapped in for the middle of the following word

parts.note: velvet is a fabric with a soft smooth pile
taken as written

explanation.surface: A research department develops a blue-green coating for a soft, smooth finish.
explanation.walkthrough: R&D is research and development; its two letters take the place of the middle LV of VELVET.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdet is verdigris, the blue-green copper acetate pigment that forms on copper and is used in paints.

clue.text: Garden pest, tail-first, gets into middle of molecast produced by soil

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so the pest goes between the central letters
putting the tail first means the last letter is moved round to the front

parts.note: an aphid is a sap-sucking insect pest

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, which alone are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of molecast

explanation.surface: A garden pest burrows into the middle of a molehill, the work of the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: A molecast is a molehill. APHID with its D brought to the front sits between E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Edaphic describes things relating to or determined by soil conditions rather than climate.
